sentences.text: The captioned appeal is by the claimants assailing the compensation determined by the Tribunal in MVC.No.323/2016.
The respondent No.2/Insurance NC: 2024:KHC-K:8296 company admits its liability.

Therefore, the appeal is purely on quantum.
2.
The claimants have filed a claim petition for having lost one Oliyadasari Narsimlu in a road traffic accident dated 19.04.2016.

Though claimants assert that deceased was self employed in Horticulture Department and had income of Rs.20,000/- per month, the Tribunal in absence of income proof,
notionally assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- and has awarded, a sum of Rs.19,28,000/- under the head 'loss of dependency'.
Aggrieved by the compensation determined by the Tribunal, the claimants are before this Court.

sentences.text: On reassessing the evidence on record, this Court is of the view that the Tribunal infact erred in notionally assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/-.
In absence of income proof, this Court is inclined to rely on the income chart prepared by the Legal Services Authority.
The accident is of the year 2016.
Therefore, the income is assessed at Rs.8,750/- and after NC: 2024:KHC-K:8296 adding 40% towards future prospects, the income is assessed at Rs.12,250/-.

After deducting 1/4th towards personal expenses, the income is taken at Rs.9,187.5/- and by applying the multiplier of 17,
the compensation payable under the head 'loss of dependency' works out to Rs.18,74,250/-
(9,187.5x12x17).
4. Under conventional heads, a sum of Rs.1,90,000/- is awarded.

The accident is of the year 2016 and therefore, a sum of Rs.38,000/- escalation at the rate of 10% for every three years is added in terms of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors.1.
